name: couple-distributed-cantilever
reference: Benchmark F12: a load introduction. The cantilever of Benchmark B1 -- 1 m x 100 mm x 100 mm of steel, 25 mm lattice, hex8 with incompatible modes -- is loaded through a lumped point at the tip instead of a traction on the tip face. geometry.addMass puts a node at the tip centroid, constraint.couple attaches it to beam.xmax as a distributed coupling, and the whole 1 kN is applied at that one node with load.force. The oracle is the traction model beside it: a distributed coupling spreads a force at the point over the face in the weights a_i / A with a_i = the face's own lumped areas, and the consistent nodal force of a uniform traction of the same total is t a_i = (F / A) a_i, so the two assembled load vectors are the same numbers. Case cantilever-hex8-im measures -0.19011253665073974 mm at the tip with the traction, and this model reproduces it to 1e-10 relative -- only the rounding of (a_i / A) F against (F / A) a_i differs. The coupling adds no stiffness anywhere (the point's row of K is empty), so the beam is exactly as flexible as before, and the clamp carries the whole 1 kN.

checks.note: the tip deflection cantilever-hex8-im measures with the same total applied as a traction, in mm: a distributed coupling introduces exactly that load and stiffens nothing
the clamp carries the applied force; the coupling's internal force is not a reaction
the resultant: the whole 1 kN reaches the clamp
